name: Umiya Mobile Ltd
title: Umiya Mobile Ltd - 544464 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Umiya Mobile is a mobile retailer expanding store count aggressively with no capacity discipline; management guides EBITDA margin to 3% by FY28 from ~1.8-1.9%, but offers no numbers on capex, and the call shows no supply-side signals.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue reached INR8,084 crore (up 47.48%) and PAT INR9.2 crore (up ~41%), with management targeting EBITDA margin of 3% by FY28.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR8,084 crore, up about 47.48% from the prior year, with EBITDA of INR15.1 crore and PAT of INR9.2 crore versus INR5.5 crore in FY25. Smartphones remain over 96% of revenue and B2B contributes over 73% per the CFO, though the Q&A cites B2B at 26-27% of revenue, an inconsistency that needs checking. Debt-equity improved from 3.77 to 1.2 after IPO proceeds repaid loans, and current ratio is 2.39. Expansion continues into Tier 2/3 markets, with 100+ stores added since the IPO and new launches in Mumbai, Odisha and Chhattisgarh planned.

financial_highlights.change: up 47.48% vs FY25 (stated as INR600 crore in FY25)
up ~41% vs INR5.5 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (per analyst question, management did not dispute)

financial_highlights.value: more than 73% (CFO); 26-27% (analyst's figure, cited in Q&A)

segments.name: Retail / B2C stores
segments.commentary: Store network of 400+ across Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh; management says about 70% of retail sales are on EMI, and average store turnover is INR25-30 lakh per month. Retail margins are described as lower than B2B.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: CFO cites over 73% contribution in FY26; management expects B2B to reach up to 35% of revenue within three years. A separate team pitches to brands for corporate and campaign sales.

segments.name: Accessories, laptops, home appliances
segments.commentary: Management says these categories are being expanded to lift customer engagement, but no revenue figures were given.

segments.name: Own stores vs retail stores
segments.commentary: Gujarat: 186 retail and 25 own stores; Maharashtra: 129 retail and 3 own stores; Madhya Pradesh: 54 retail and 2 own stores; Daman & Diu: 3 retail stores.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to rise from ~1.8-1.9% to up to 3%, targeted in about two years (FY28), via lower expansion opex, combo/accessory attach, and vendor support of 0.5-1% based on volume.
Mumbai (Bombay) operations to start in FY26; Odisha and Chhattisgarh operations to start in 2026.
Management says expansion is the priority, with dividends only after states are covered; no plans to raise external funds, with capex to be funded internally and bank support available.
Insurance and buyback revenue at 2-3% currently, with a target of 10% in FY26 per management.
Mobile volume may decline 2% to -2% due to chipset-driven price increases; refurbished and buyback business expected to grow.
Management plans to move to the main board after three years, when SME listing lock-in ends.
capex_capacity: 100+ stores added since the IPO; expansion focus on Tier 2/3 cities.
Store break-even expected in 6-12 months; new stores set up with own COCO store and warehouse first in new states.
Inventory managed at 20 days of store stock plus 10 days of warehouse stock (28-30 days total), with a target to cut to 10 days at store level if supply is steady.
Management did not give capex figures for the next 18-24 months; asked whether 100-150 more stores in 12-18 months would be significant, management said it would be done internally.
demand_pricing: Management says online and offline prices now largely match because of brand tie-ups tied to store volume; offline offers include cashback, exchange, buyback, EMI-free months and bank tie-ups.
Per management, new mobile volume may fall 2% to -2% under chipset-driven price rises; the shift toward refurbished and exchange is aimed at keeping consumers buying.
Dead stock estimated at 1-2% of brand inventory; management claims Umiya carries no dead stock because of an aging team.
MOP margin on phones stated at around 9-10%, with a Indore launch offer of free cycles and a INR4-5 lakh launch spend per store.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term strategy against e-commerce, and how is Umiya's price competitive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said online and Umiya prices now match on most models because brand tie-ups tied to volume give Umiya the same rates. Exchange, buyback, cashback and touch-and-feel are cited as the reasons customers buy offline. Expansion in Tier 2/3 cities is the stated response.

qa_highlights.question: How will B2B grow and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B could reach up to 35% of revenue in three years. Margin levers are lower expansion opex, combo offers, and vendor support of 0.5-1%, with EBITDA margin targeted at up to 3% in about two years (FY28).

qa_highlights.question: What is the EMI mix and the store strategy in new states?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of sales are on EMI, including card, finance and UPI cashback. New states start with a 1-2 month recce, then a COCO store and warehouse before franchise expansion. Break-even is 6-12 months per store.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise capital or pay dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: No external fundraise is planned and expansion is funded internally. Dividends will come only after states are covered. Management said the bank approaches it upfront.

qa_highlights.question: How are insurance and buyback contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance and buyback are running at 2-3% of revenue; the target is 10% in FY26. Management said refurbished stock and exchange are being pushed more as phone prices rise.

risks_watch: Data inconsistency: CFO says B2B is over 73% of revenue, while the analyst's figure of 26-27% was not corrected on the call.
Management cited the EBITDA margin of 1.8-1.9% without a disclosed base; the 3% target depends on opex reductions and vendor support that are not quantified.
Expansion to Mumbai, Odisha and Chhattisgarh and 100-150 more stores in 12-18 months, funded internally, with no capex figures given.
Competition from online pricing and festival-period exclusive tie-ups that can break price parity for one or two days.
Stock price decline over the last five to six months, which management attributed to the post-IPO deployment period.
Website store counts appeared outdated; management said it would be updated.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansion-focused on store growth and margin levers, with the CFO's numbers stated firmly. Answers on margins, B2B mix and capex were broad and not quantified, and several answers were vague or repetitive on specific numbers.
key_quotes: Today, online and Umiya's prices are similar, or Umiya's price is far better and lower than online.
So, we manage with a 28 to 30 days stock inventory, and it's a complete ERP based on sales, we call it DOS.
For now, we will manage it internally. Right now, we have no plan to take funds from outside or anything like that.

adds.what: 100+ retail stores added since IPO (Tier 2/3 focus)
New state operations in Mumbai, Odisha and Chhattisgarh

growth.why: Management guides EBITDA margin up to 3% by FY28 (from ~1.8-1.9%) and B2B to 35% in three years, backed by 100+ stores added since IPO, new state launches in 2026 and vendor support of 0.5-1%, but no capex figures or order book were given and the B2B share (73% vs 26-27%) is inconsistent.
